correctness.rationale: For every prime \(p=6m+5\), direct Cartier \(p^{-1}\)-linear coefficient extraction on the explicit regular differential basis gives precisely two potentially nonzero entries Q and P. The polynomial ODE and exact conjugation identity \(L_{\mathrm{big}}(D^{m+1}Q)=D^{m+1}L_{\mathrm{small}}(Q)-8(m+1)pD^mQ\), plus uniqueness by nonzero coefficient recurrence, prove \(P=cD^{m+1}Q\) in all characteristics. Q has exact degree m, is nonzero at \(a=\pm2\), and the same regular differential equation makes repeated roots impossible because \(m<p\). Thus exactly m smooth superspecial parameters. The nonzero \(2\times2\) semilinear Cartier swap has stable rank 2, determining the complementary \(p\)-rank and Newton slopes. In \(p\equiv1\pmod3\), the ordinary \(j=0\) elliptic quotient prevents superspeciality. Laga–Shnidman’s complete geometric invariant \(j=1-a^2/4\) yields the class count. The standalone polynomial verifier, run from packaged source, checks 23 primes \(p<200\) and exact examples; these computations are separate from the all-prime proof.

evidence: Laga–Shnidman, arxiv:2308.15297, §2.3, studies exactly \(y^3=x^4+ax^2+b\) and classifies geometric isomorphism by \((4b-a^2)/(4b)\).

broader_coverage.reasoning: The exact geometric family is covered in its definition and moduli, but not its positive-characteristic all-prime superspecial intersection. A global listing algorithm and small-p tables do not imply this closed-form identity, root separability, or count for unbounded p. The cited constant-rank proposition is contradicted by a direct computation and thus cannot dominate the new theorem.

originality.rationale: After actual semantic record searches and closest full-text comparisons, the uniform all-prime squarefree coefficient identity, exact superspecial root and geometric-class count, and complementary Newton stratum are not supplied by the available primary sources. General Cartier coefficient formulas are known, and special \(a=0\) Fermat cases are known; neither directly proves the asserted uniform root count. Nourozi–Rahmati’s general constant-rank assertion is in tension with the classical superspecial examples and directly calculated characteristic-17 exceptions and therefore does not constitute correct dominating coverage. Priority remains provisional, particularly because the relevant 1991 full text could not be inspected.
residual_risks: The 1991 Estrada-Sarlabous full body was not accessible; it may contain an equivalent specialization or stronger formula not visible in its abstract.
Indexed sections rather than whole full text were read for the 2015 Kazemifard–Tafazolian publisher article.
Historical priority is provisional; unindexed subsequent literature or finite-field databases may hold equivalent classifications.
Nourozi–Rahmati’s published constant-\(a\)-number claim is directly in tension with proven special cases; an independent expert should assess that comparison.

value.rationale: The superspecial intersection of the natural one-dimensional bielliptic Picard locus with genus-three superspecial moduli is intrinsically meaningful. A uniform all-prime exact intersection degree, simple-root/transversality statement, full complementary Newton stratum, and count of geometric isomorphism classes provide reusable structural information beyond isolated numerical examples or known special Fermat reductions. The result concerns a natural invariant, not an arbitrary polynomial slice.
